rawFindings.title: `baseDirFromPattern` now drops non-glob paths containing `+(` in the directory name
rawFindings.explanation: The new regex treats any `/(...)+(` sequence as glob syntax, even when `+(` appears in a literal folder name. For example, a config pattern like `/tmp/a+(old)/**/*.js` is converted to `/tmp`, so the watcher no longer watches the actual directory tree and file changes under `/tmp/a+(old)` are missed.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restrict the special-case stripping to actual extglob syntax by matching only segments that begin with `+(` or `!(` immediately after a path separator and are followed by a closing `)`/trailing glob characters, or use a real glob parser instead of ad hoc regexes.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With a watched pattern of `/tmp/a+(old)/**/*.js`, chokidar is started on `/tmp` instead of `/tmp/a+(old)`, so edits under `/tmp/a+(old)/src/app.js` do not trigger `add/change/unlink` events.

rawFindings.title: `baseDirFromPattern` now drops non-glob paths containing `?` after a `)` in directory names
rawFindings.explanation: The added `\)\?` rule also matches literal folder names that contain `)?`, not just optional-group glob syntax. A path such as `/tmp/report)?archive/*.js` is reduced to `/tmp`, so the watcher registers the wrong parent directory and ignores changes in the intended folder.
rawFindings.suggestion: Only strip `(...)?` when the `)` and `?` are part of an extglob segment, not when they occur in a literal path component; alternatively, delegate this normalization to a glob-aware utility.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With a watched pattern of `/tmp/report)?archive/*.js`, the watcher is added for `/tmp` rather than `/tmp/report)?archive`, so creating `/tmp/report)?archive/index.js` never reaches the watcher callbacks.
